key_insight: The paper shows that encoder--decoder operator learning can be analyzed at a resolution-independent level by passing to a limiting kernel, so learning guarantees no longer depend on the particular finite discretization.
engineering_relevance: This gives a principled way to design and analyze mesh-, grid-, or basis-based operator-learning systems, including neural operator models, with sample and parameter complexity guarantees that remain valid as resolution increases.
method: Construct an induced operator-valued kernel from a matrix-valued kernel on the encoded space and show the RKHSs are isometrically isomorphic.
Prove convergence of induced kernels to a limiting kernel via operator-norm convergence of their integral operators.
Derive upper and lower error bounds for regularized SGD and extend the analysis to encoder--decoder neural networks through the limiting NTK.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence and error bounds, including upper/lower bounds for SGD and polynomial complexity guarantees for encoder--decoder neural networks, but does not mention experiments.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on how fast encoding errors decay and may weaken when finite-width, finite-sample, or discretization errors are not sufficiently small.
paper_title: Resolution-Independent Analysis of Encoder--Decoder Operator Learning via Limiting Kernels
